=== owners.POST.yml ===
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkDailyLimit

checkDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerDailyLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkCityCapacity

checkCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkIdentityUnique

# Consolidated duplicate detection: reject with 409 only when the new owner's whole
# identityKey (normalized telephone | email | householdId) matches an existing owner's.
# Runs after assignHousehold so the new owner already carries any shared householdId.
checkIdentityUnique:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerIdentityUnique
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignPossibleDuplicate

# Soft-match: not a hard duplicate (identityKey unique) but shares an existing owner's
# lastName and postcode with a different telephone -> still created, flagged with
# possibleDuplicate=true and possibleDuplicateOf=<matching owner id>.
assignPossibleDuplicate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignPossibleDuplicate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHouseholdSize

assignHouseholdSize:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHouseholdSize
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCustomerCode

assignCustomerCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignNamesakeCount

assignNamesakeCount:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignBulkSignupWarning

assignBulkSignupWarning:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignBulkSignupWarning
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

audit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AuditOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

## Summary

I implemented the disposable-domain blocklist rule for owner email, following the project's OfficeFloor function-injection conventions.

**Change:** Reject `POST /api/owners` (and `PUT /api/owners/{ownerId}`) with **400** when the email's domain is `mailinator.com`, `tempmail.com`, or `guerrillamail.com`.

**Files:**
- `function/owner/OwnerEmail.java` — added a `DISPOSABLE_DOMAINS` set; after the syntax check, `normalize(...)` extracts the domain and throws the new exception when it's blocklisted. Placing it here means both create (`ValidateOwnerFields`) and update (`ApplyOwner`) paths enforce it.
- `escalation/OwnerEmailDisposableException.java` — new checked exception (mirrors `OwnerEmailInvalidException`).
- `escalation/OwnerEmailDisposableExceptionHandler.java` — responds `400` with `{"errors":["email"]}`, matching the existing invalid-email handler.
- `officefloor/escalation/...OwnerEmailDisposableException.yml` — wires the handler.
- `ValidateOwnerFields.java` / `ApplyOwner.java` — added the new exception to their `throws` clauses (required for OfficeFloor escalation).

The check compares the domain lower-cased (post-normalization), so `X@Mailinator.com` is also blocked, while syntactically-valid non-blocklisted addresses continue to pass.
